label: History
value: Clementine sent John Ashdown a formal rejection.
unit: Rev. John Ashdown served as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes church, living at the aged gray manse in Juneford with his children and Aunt Martha following the sudden death of his beloved wife Cecilia. Often lost in academic reading and theological dilemmas, he frequently neglected his daily routine and pastoral duties, once even confusing burial rites during a wedding ceremony. During a walk through Fern Hollow, he struck up a deep, intimate friendship with Edmund Carrow and later encountered Clementine Ainslie, whose beauty and maternal nature gradually won his heart. After a harsh confrontation with Mrs. Twiss over his neglect as a father, Ashdown wrestled with his shortcomings and sought counsel from Mrs. Carrow. Eventually realizing his love for Clementine, he proposed to her; however, she sent him a formal rejection, leaving him heartbroken and convinced he could never love another woman. Struggling with his duties, he later agonized over having to discipline his son Rupert, unable to bring himself to carry out the punishment.

value: When dealing with misconduct, Thorne sets appropriate standards.
unit: Miss Thorne is an intelligent, compassionate, and open-minded educator who manages her classroom with tact and attentive direction. She successfully draws out her pupils' finest moral and intellectual qualities and gains their deep affection without ever resorting to striking them. When dealing with misconduct, she forgives readily while firmly addressing dishonest behavior and setting appropriate standards.

My reading of it began during the lunch hour, and the chariot race had just been reached when classes resumed. I was desperate to learn the result—even though I felt certain that Ben Hur was bound to win, as it would lack poetical justice otherwise—which led me to lay the history book open upon the top of my desk and wedge Ben Hur underneath it against my knee. He grew up deeply attached to Fern Hollow, hanging sleigh-bells on the tangled Tree Lovers trees and frequently foraging and fishing there. He gained a reputation at school as a chieftain who engaged in sports and fights, contrasting with his brother Edmund. While visiting Grey Shutters, he became the most cherished child of Aunt Thirza. Later, he showed Mary Stubbs his inherited collection of oddities in the Hollowmere attic and showed great competence in handling her outbursts. As he matured, he began preparing for the entrance examination for Regent's Academy by staying after school and studying in the garret, gradually spending less evening time in Fern Hollow. Prior to leaving for Port Marlow to attend the Academy, he shared a final evening gathering in Fern Hollow with his companions and expressed a deep yearning to become a famous soldier and general.

label: History
value: Agatha Sowerby led church societies.
unit: Living at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent decades as a central figure in the community, leading church societies and keeping a watchful eye over her neighbors. When Nell Harcourt first arrived at Grey Shutters, Mrs. Agatha criticized her appearance, sparking a fierce outburst from Nell; however, after Nell offered a humble apology, Mrs. Agatha quickly forgave her. Over time, she grew fond of Nell and actively assisted her and the Abernethys, including dressmaking for Nell and managing various church events. When her husband Thomas fell sick and died, Mrs. Agatha nursed him devotedly; facing financial hardship and the sale of her farm, she accepted Thirza Abernethy's invitation to move into Grey Shutters rather than leave Brierley. At Grey Shutters, she remained deeply involved in parish affairs and community gossip while helping raise the children. In her later years, she continued to reside at Grey Shutters, occupying her time by crafting cotton-warp quilts for Nell's future daughters.
